simple.meaning: זָכוּר (zâkûwr) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a male (of man or animals).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Exodus, Deuteronomy, beginning at Exodus 23:17. Its contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זָכוּר (H2138).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.full: H2138. zakur [ זָכוּר ] noun masculine male , i. q. זָכָר , but only with suffix; — collective כָּלזְֿכוּרְךָ Exod 23:17 = 34:23 (both J E), = Deut 16:16 , of attendance at feasts; כָּלזְֿכוּרָהּ (of city refusing terms of peace) 20:13 commanded to be slain (opposed to הַטַּף הַנָּשִׁים, , etc., 20:14 ).
definitions.rootNote: properly, passive participle of 2142 , but used for 2145 ;

occurrences.englishText: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord Yahweh.
Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord Yahweh, the God of Israel.

Three times in a year all of your males shall appear before Yahweh your God in the place which he chooses: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of booths. They shall not appear before Yahweh empty.
When Yahweh your God delivers it into your hand, you shall strike every male of it with the edge of the sword;
